title.narrative: Reintegration for Liberian returnees through skills training and job creation

description.narrative: Following a decade of peace in Liberia, the international community invoked the Cessation Clause on 30 June 2012 ending the refugee status of the Liberians who fled their country during the two civil wars between 1989 and 2003, which tore the country apart killing more than 250,000 people and forcing some 750,000 to leave their homes. Most of those who fled during the two periods of conflict sought shelter in the neighbouring countries including, Cote d#Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Nigeria, Sierra Leone and Gambia. As a result of the cessation, 2012 has seen a surge in the number of returnees with about 29,380 Liberians going back home doubling the initial estimate of 15,000 for that same year. By the end of 2012, UNHCR completed a voluntary repatriation of more than 155,000 Liberians after 23 years from the start of the civil war. Most of the returnees are likely to have temporary settled down in and around Monrovia. While Liberia is on the way to recovery, the fragile post-conflict setting puts an enormous burden to the country in reintegrating the returnees and providing them with opportunities to secure viable and dignified livelihoods.
